scope.historicalEvidence: Earlier 2026-10-30 records and canvas-freeze-allocation-2026-11-02.json are unchanged. Initial, prototype and final phases below retain their own recorded artifact fingerprints; they are not interchangeable.

defaultCorrectnessFixes: Use a store-wide monotonically increasing Long source version serial, so unregister/re-register of one logical texture id cannot alias an in-flight old version or fool cached parent dependencies.
Include alphaBleedRequired in ordinary and shared pixel registration stamps; alpha bleed, premultiplication and dimensions remain distinct semantics, including when sharing is disabled.

RWX_SHARE_TEXTURE_REGISTRATIONS.behavior: Share source pixel registration stamps between a root, its detached engine and child targets. Published resources, leases and fence owners remain separate.
RWX_SHARE_TEXTURE_REGISTRATIONS.harnessRequirement: Requested live/replay candidate must emit the marker; omitted flag pins the candidate to 0.

RWX_FROZEN_CONTENT_REUSE.behavior: Existing complete dependency/resource-closure reuse candidate. The new per-frame-traversal identity/scope memo only reduces repeated dependency contributions while this candidate is enabled. First resolution and resource graph construction remain unchanged.

productionChanges.versionPolicy: This is the same 1.4.3 batch; no additional application-version increment, protocol/replay-version change or release package in this follow-up.

freeze.static: Both update intervals default to zero: timed work remains freezeFrame plus lease close.
freeze.dynamic: --update-every=N re-records/registers one round-robin GPU target; --source-update-every=N commits/registers one changed leaf sprite before that iteration freeze. Iterations span warmup and measurement continuously.
freeze.replacement: Updated target recording begins with explicit Clear, preventing persistent-target command accumulation.
freeze.validation: Outside timing, verify actual commands, pixel values, frozen-version changes, exact update counts and old lease stability; one additional old lease is retained during dynamic timing. Resource counts alone are insufficient.

renderer.scope: Only prebuilt-command CPU dispatch and mesh/instance/material object construction. Recording/freezing, shader compilation, GPU execution and presentation are excluded.
renderer.validation: All synthetic phases compare draw order, counts, bindings, raw geometry/instance bits and indices before and after timing; geometry digests are also compared across independent JVMs.

limits: CPU-only synthetic screening with user work continuing; not end-to-end or original-client parity.

protocol.scope: dynamic recording, registration, freeze and lease close; no GPU/presentation
CPU freeze/lease plus requested rerecording and source registration; no GPU/presentation.

decisions.initialScreen: 32 retained records tested four freeze cases and four renderer flags individually on the earlier core. Static reuse helped strongly, but source churn reversed the result; these are not final-core or end-to-end results.
decisions.alwaysSharedPrototype: 8 retained before/after records: with frozen reuse OFF, CPU rose 31.03%; with reuse ON, CPU fell 80.51%. This demonstrated interaction between candidate settings, so the final shared-registration option is separately controlled and currently default OFF. Actual-gameplay and official-client acceptance remain outstanding; the per-frame shared-source rewrite extreme is not a hard gate.
decisions.finalCombination: On the same final core, compare both flags OFF against both ON. Static allocation fell 87.00%; one cell update per frame plus one source update per 16 frames fell 63.06% in allocation and 58.36% in CPU. Source updated every frame increased allocation 104.21% and CPU 72.81%; retain that extreme synthetic case as diagnostic/history only, not an acceptance or default-enablement veto. Candidates remain default OFF pending actual-gameplay and unmodified-official-client comparison; synthetic wins do not establish parity.
decisions.rendererCandidates: Map slots reduced allocation 49.71% with CPU about -1.00%; texture material reuse reduced allocation 42.72% and CPU 10.92%; compact quads increased CPU 8.31%, compact instances increased allocation 3.06%. All remain separately controlled candidates, with no GPU or interaction acceptance.
